Name: Generate the mesh
Description: Finds walkable ground the nav mesh is missing - rooftops, lift platforms, ground on top of props, and other spots the game's own generator skipped - and adds it. If there's no .nav file yet, this builds one from scratch instead.
Warning: Experimental. Adds areas that have not been verified in game; review the result before shipping it.

Name: Start from scratch
Description: Throws away the existing nav mesh and builds a new one from the map's player spawns, instead of just filling in the missing parts. Only works together with "Generate the mesh".
Warning: Destructive. Deletes every area, ladder and hand placement already in the .nav beside the BSP. Back it up first if you want to keep it.

Name: Counter-Strike movement limits
Description: Use Counter-Strike's movement limits - a 58 unit crouch jump, a 200 unit survivable drop and a 58 unit climb - instead of the defaults that suit Garry's Mod, HL2 and TF2 (64, 400 and 200). It is not cosmetic: the same map generates around 100 fewer areas under Counter-Strike's limits, because a ledge 62 units up stops being climbable.
Warning: Only for Counter-Strike games. Setting it elsewhere throws away routes that game's players can actually take.

Name: Skip ladders
Description: Skip building nav ladders for the map's ladder brushes. The engine builds none of these outside Left 4 Dead, so skipping this leaves brush ladders invisible to bots.

Name: Skip movement
Description: Don't mark stairs or add step, jump, drop and lift connections.

Name: Delete unreachable areas
Description: Delete small groups of areas no player spawn can walk to - the stray samples the generator leaves inside sealed geometry, such as the nodraw top of a brush under a walkway. Off by default: measured against the mesh the game generates for the same map, most unreachable ground is real ground that simply did not get linked, and deleting it loses more than it cleans up. The count is reported either way.
Warning: Destructive. Removes areas from the mesh; large stranded groups are always left alone.

Name: Skip cover spots
Description: Skip finding hiding spots, grading sniper spots and building encounter spots. The game computes hiding spots during its own nav_generate, so a mesh without them is missing something it expects to find.

Name: Skip sniper spot grading
Description: Find cover spots but don't grade which of them are good or ideal sniper positions. This is the more expensive half of the cover work - every spot is traced against the whole mesh.

Name: Skip encounter spots
Description: Find cover spots but don't work out which of them are visible along each route between areas.

Name: Skip visibility
Description: Skip working out which areas can see each other. This is by far the slowest step - roughly two thirds of a full run - and skipping it leaves bots less aware of good hiding and ambush spots.

Name: Max view distance
Description: How far apart two areas can be and still count as able to see each other. Lower values compile faster but bots lose some long-range awareness.

Name: Do not compress visibility
Description: Store the full visibility data instead of the engine's delta encoding. Roughly doubles the file size; mainly useful for debugging.

Name: Thread limit
Description: Limit how many CPU cores Meshwright uses. Leave this off to use all of them - useful if you want to keep using your computer for other things during a long compile.

Name: Write to a different file
Description: Write the finished mesh somewhere other than over the .nav beside the BSP. Useful for comparing a generated mesh against the one you already have.
